dialogue.speaker: Pip
dialogue.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: Do you know what I touch here?

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

dialogue.speaker: Pip
dialogue.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

dialogue.speaker: Miss Havisham
dialogue.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

Miss Havisham.name: Miss Havisham
Miss Havisham.description: A wealthy, eccentric woman who has isolated herself from the world after a betrayal. She is dressed in an old wedding gown and her room is filled with reminders of her past, including stopped clocks.

Pip.name: Pip
Pip.description: A young boy who is brought to Miss Havisham's estate by Mr. Pumblechook to entertain her. He is confused and uncomfortable in the strange and melancholic environment.

context: Pip, a young boy, is brought to Miss Havisham's isolated estate to entertain her. Miss Havisham, a reclusive and bitter woman, is seeking diversion and has a peculiar interest in Pip.
